rag.name: LO.Modal.NNFormula
rag.content:
inductive NNFormula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | atom   : α → NNFormula α
  | natom  : α → NNFormula α
  | falsum : NNFormula α
  | verum  : NNFormula α
  | or     : NNFormula α → NNFormula α → NNFormula α
  | and    : NNFormula α → NNFormula α → NNFormula α
  | box    : NNFormula α → NNFormula α
  | dia    : NNFormula α → NNFormula α
  deriving DecidableEq

rag.name: LO.Modal.NNFormula.cases'
rag.content:
@[elab_as_elim]
def cases'
  {C : NNFormula α → Sort v}
  (hAtom   : ∀ a, C (atom a))
  (hNatom  : ∀ a, C (natom a))
  (hFalsum : C ⊥)
  (hVerum  : C ⊤)
  (hOr     : ∀ φ ψ, C (φ ⋎ ψ))
  (hAnd    : ∀ φ ψ, C (φ ⋏ ψ))
  (hBox    : ∀ φ, C (□φ))
  (hDia    : ∀ φ, C (◇φ))
  : ∀ φ, C φ
  | atom a  => hAtom a
  | natom a => hNatom a
  | ⊥  => hFalsum
  | ⊤   => hVerum
  | φ ⋎ ψ => hOr φ ψ
  | φ ⋏ ψ => hAnd φ ψ
  | □φ => hBox φ
  | ◇φ => hDia φ

rag.name: LO.Modal.NNFormula.ofNat
rag.content:
def ofNat : Nat → Option (NNFormula α)
  | 0 => none
  | e + 1 =>
    let idx := e.unpair.1
    let c := e.unpair.2
    match idx with
    | 0 => some ⊥
    | 1 => some ⊤
    | 2 => (decode c).map NNFormula.atom
    | 3 => (decode c).map NNFormula.natom
    | 4 =>
      have : c.unpair.1 < e + 1 := Nat.lt_succ.mpr $ le_trans (Nat.unpair_left_le _) $ Nat.unpair_right_le _
      have : c.unpair.2 < e + 1 := Nat.lt_succ.mpr $ le_trans (Nat.unpair_right_le _) $ Nat.unpair_right_le _
      do
        let φ ← ofNat c.unpair.1
        let ψ ← ofNat c.unpair.2
        return φ ⋎ ψ
    | 5 =>
      have : c.unpair.1 < e + 1 := Nat.lt_succ.mpr $ le_trans (Nat.unpair_left_le _) $ Nat.unpair_right_le _
      have : c.unpair.2 < e + 1 := Nat.lt_succ.mpr $ le_trans (Nat.unpair_right_le _) $ Nat.unpair_right_le _
      do
        let φ ← ofNat c.unpair.1
        let ψ ← ofNat c.unpair.2
        return φ ⋏ ψ
    | 6 =>
      have : c < e + 1 := Nat.lt_succ.mpr $ Nat.unpair_right_le _
      do
        let φ ← ofNat c;
        return □φ
    | 7 =>
      have : c < e + 1 := Nat.lt_succ.mpr $ Nat.unpair_right_le _
      do
        let φ ← ofNat c;
        return ◇φ
    | _ => none

informal_statement: For any natural number \( a \), a structure \( x \) satisfies the atomic formula \( \text{natom}(a) \) if and only if \( a \) is not in \( x \).
informal_proof:
To prove the statement, we rely on the definitions of satisfaction and models in the context of structures and atomic formulas.

By definition, \( \text{natom}(a) \) represents the negation of the atomic formula associated with \( a \). The satisfaction condition \( x \models \text{natom}(a) \) thus captures the scenario where \( x \) does not satisfy the atomic formula \( a \), which is precisely expressed by \( \neg M x a \). This equivalence is directly derived from the foundational definitions of the `Satisfies` class and its `iff_models` property.

Therefore, the proof follows straightforwardly by unpacking these definitions, confirming that \( x \models \text{natom}(a) \) holds exactly when \( a \) is not an element of \( x \).
